questions.prompt: Why can GeoDNS send a Madrid user to Amsterdam?
options: DNS sees the resolver's location, not the user's

questions.prompt: Why is failing over a region by changing DNS slow?
options: Answers are cached, and some clients ignore short TTLs
Many locations announce the same IP, and routers send packets along the shortest path

questions.prompt: Anycast spreads a DDoS attack across every location instead of concentrating it on one.
What's the acronym for a CDN or cloud edge location near users? (three letters)
Three regions each run at 70%. One fails, and its traffic splits evenly over the other two. What happens?
options: They hit 105%: a regional failure becomes a global overload
Deliberately rejecting low-priority work when overloaded
